blocks.h2: How an Overhead Sewer System Works
blocks.body: Every drain below the street sewer's flow line, like your floor drain, a basement bathroom, or a laundry line, normally relies on gravity to reach the sewer. An overhead sewer system reroutes those drains into a sump pit instead. An [ejector pump](/mokena/ejector-pump) lifts that wastewater up to a line above flood level, where a check valve keeps it from flowing back down. From there, gravity carries it the rest of the way to the street sewer, the same as every drain upstairs.

blocks.intro: In August 2025, storms dropped 4 to 8 inches of rain across the region, and the National Weather Service reported significant flash flooding in Mokena.

items.body: A lot of Mokena homes built in the 1990s and 2000s have finished basements. They're the ones most worth protecting.

blocks.h2: Flood Control Questions From Mokena Homeowners

items.q: What is a flood control system?
items.preview: Usually an overhead sewer, a backflow valve or both.
items.answer: It's a setup that keeps sewer water from coming into your basement. In most Mokena homes, that means an overhead sewer system, a backflow valve or a combination.

items.q: Does an overhead sewer stop groundwater?
items.preview: No. That's the sump pump's job.
items.answer: No. It stops sewer backups. Groundwater around the foundation needs a [sump pump](/mokena/sump-pumps).

items.q: Can we keep our basement bathroom?
items.answer: Yes. The bathroom drains to the new pit along with the rest of the basement.
Usually a few days, depending on the layout and how much of the basement is finished.

items.q: How much does a flood control system cost in Mokena?
items.preview: It depends on your basement. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the depth of the sewer, the layout, the fixtures and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
